taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, both regions are still on daylight saving time:

- **Eastern Time** is EDT (UTC−4). US daylight saving time ends November 1, 2026.
- **Madrid** is CEST (UTC+2). EU summer time ends October 25, 2026.

So 5:00 PM EDT is 21:00 UTC, which is **11:00 PM in Madrid** the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is **UTC−5** all year. Peru does not observe daylight saving time.

12:00 UTC − 5 hours = **07:00 in Lima** on the same day, July 15, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, so 9:00 AM CEST is 07:00 UTC. Tokyo uses JST (UTC+9) all year with no daylight saving time, so you add 9 hours: 07:00 UTC is 16:00 JST on the same day.

The deadline is **4:00 PM on June 1, 2026**, Tokyo time.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **8:59 AM on Monday, October 12, 2026**, in Madrid.

- **PDT is UTC−7.** US daylight saving time runs until November 1, 2026, so it still applies on October 11.
- **Madrid is on CEST, UTC+2.** EU summer time runs until October 25, 2026.
- **Madrid is 9 hours ahead.** 23:59 PDT on October 11 is 06:59 UTC on October 12, which is 08:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 3, 2026, Los Angeles is still on Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8), because US daylight saving time starts on March 8. Madrid is on Central European Time (UTC+1), because EU daylight saving time starts on March 29. That puts Madrid 9 hours ahead.

- 11:59 PM PST on March 3 = 07:59 UTC on March 4
- 07:59 UTC = 08:59 in Madrid on March 4

The deadline is Wednesday, March 4, 2026, at 08:59 your time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In February, Central European Time is standard time (UTC+1), and Los Angeles is on Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8). That puts Los Angeles 9 hours behind CET.

- 10:00 CET on Feb 2 is 09:00 UTC.
- 09:00 UTC is 01:00 PST on Feb 2.

The deadline is 1:00 AM on February 2, 2026, in Los Angeles. That is very early on the morning of Feb 2, so if you're planning to submit "on Feb 2," you should submit by the evening of Feb 1.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time is UTC+9, and Lima is UTC−5 all year, since Peru doesn't observe daylight saving time. Lima is therefore 14 hours behind Japan.

- 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 is 23:00 UTC on May 4.
- 23:00 UTC minus 5 hours is 18:00 (6:00 PM) on May 4 in Lima.

So you need to submit by 6:00 PM on Monday, May 4, 2026, Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **7:59 AM on Thursday, October 29, 2026**, Madrid time.

- On October 28, 2026, Pacific Time is still on daylight saving time (PDT, UTC−7). US clocks don't fall back until November 1, 2026.
- Madrid has already left summer time by then. Europe falls back on October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
- That makes the gap 8 hours instead of the usual 9.
- So 11:59 PM PDT on October 28 is 06:59 UTC on October 29, which is 07:59 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The session starts at **2:00 PM (14:00) on October 30, 2026, Madrid time**.

- **New York:** US daylight saving time ends on November 1, 2026. On October 30, Eastern Time is still EDT (UTC−4). So 9:00 AM ET = 13:00 UTC.
- **Madrid:** Europe's daylight saving time ends on October 25, 2026. On October 30, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). So 13:00 UTC = 14:00 local.

The usual gap between Madrid and New York is 6 hours. During this week it is only 5 hours, because the two regions switch clocks on different dates.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **1:00 PM (13:00) on October 27, 2026** in New York.

- **CET** is UTC+1. Europe leaves summer time on October 25, 2026, so standard CET applies on October 27. 18:00 CET is 17:00 UTC.
- **New York** stays on daylight time (EDT, UTC−4) until November 1, 2026. 17:00 UTC is 13:00 EDT.

For this week only, the gap is 5 hours instead of the usual 6, because Europe changes its clocks a week before the US.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **8:59 AM on Tuesday, November 3, 2026**, Madrid time.

- **Pacific Time:** US daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. On November 2, "PT" therefore means PST, which is UTC−8.
- **Madrid:** Europe's summer time ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. On these dates Madrid is on CET, which is UTC+1.
- **Difference:** Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT on these dates.
- **Conversion:** 11:59 PM PST on Nov 2 is 07:59 UTC on Nov 3, which is 08:59 CET on Nov 3.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **Saturday, March 21, 2026 at 07:59** in Madrid.

- **Pacific Time:** The US switches to daylight time on March 8, 2026. On March 20, PT is PDT, which is UTC−7.
- **Madrid:** Spain does not switch to summer time until March 29, 2026. On that date, Madrid is on CET, which is UTC+1.
- **Difference:** Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT.

March 20 at 23:59 PDT is March 21 at 06:59 UTC, which is March 21 at 07:59 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The webinar starts at **4:00 AM PDT on March 25, 2026**.

- **CET:** On March 25, 2026, Central Europe is still on standard time (CET, UTC+1), because EU summer time begins March 29, 2026. So 12:00 PM CET is 11:00 UTC.
- **Los Angeles:** US daylight saving time began March 8, 2026, so Los Angeles is on PDT (UTC−7). 11:00 UTC minus 7 hours is 04:00 PDT.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Deadline in Madrid: Monday, October 12, 2026 at 06:00**

- **"12:00 AM" means midnight at the start of the day.** So 12:00 AM on October 12 is the moment October 11 ends and October 12 begins (00:00 on Oct 12).
- **Eastern Time on that date is EDT (UTC−4).** US daylight saving time runs until November 1, 2026.
- **Madrid on that date is CEST (UTC+2).** European summer time runs until October 25, 2026.
- **The difference is 6 hours, with Madrid ahead.** 00:00 EDT = 04:00 UTC = 06:00 in Madrid.

"12:00 AM" deadlines are often misread. If the organizers actually meant the end of October 12 (midnight going into October 13), the deadline would be **October 13 at 06:00** Madrid time. To be safe, submit before the earlier time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 13:59** in Madrid.

- **AoE ("Anywhere on Earth")** is UTC−12. So 23:59 AoE on October 9 is **11:59 UTC on October 10**.
- **Madrid** is still on summer time (CEST, UTC+2) on October 10, 2026. Summer time ends there on October 25.
- 11:59 UTC + 2 hours = **13:59 local time on October 10**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In mid-August, Pacific Time is on daylight saving time (PDT, UTC−7), and Madrid is on summer time (CEST, UTC+2). That puts Madrid 9 hours ahead.

12:00 PM PDT on August 14 = 19:00 UTC = **21:00 in Madrid** on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **7:29 PM on November 10, 2026**, Madrid time, assuming IST means India Standard Time.

- **India Standard Time (IST)** is UTC+5:30, so 23:59 IST = 18:29 UTC.
- **Madrid** will be on Central European Time (UTC+1) by November 10, since daylight saving time ends on October 25, 2026. So 18:29 UTC = 19:29 in Madrid.

**About the abbreviation:** "IST" can also mean Israel Standard Time (UTC+2), which would make the deadline 22:59 Madrid time. It can also mean Irish Standard Time, but Ireland uses that only in summer, so it doesn't apply in November. If the contest is Israeli, check with the organizers.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time is UTC+5:45, and Lima (Peru Time) is UTC−5:00. Neither observes daylight saving time.

- 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2 is 11:15 UTC.
- 11:15 UTC minus 5 hours is 6:15 AM in Lima.

The deadline is 6:15 AM on April 2, 2026, Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is **01:30 on Tuesday, October 6, 2026**, Madrid time.

1. **Adelaide's offset:** South Australia starts daylight saving on the first Sunday of October. In 2026 that is October 4. So on October 6, Adelaide is on ACDT, which is UTC+10:30.
   10:00 ACDT = **23:30 UTC on October 5**.

2. **Madrid's offset:** Spain stays on summer time (CEST, UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October, which is October 25 in 2026.
   23:30 UTC + 2 hours = **01:30 on October 6**.

This is in the early hours of the same calendar date shown on the contest page. In practice, you should submit by the evening of Monday, October 5.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Sydney:** Daylight saving starts on the first Sunday of October, which is October 4, 2026. On October 3, Sydney is still on standard time (AEST, UTC+10). 6:00 PM AEST is 08:00 UTC.

**Madrid:** Summer time runs until the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so on October 3 Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2). 08:00 UTC is 10:00 in Madrid.

The deadline is 10:00 AM on Saturday, October 3, 2026, Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
